cell_types.name: Cardiomyocytes (ventricular-like)
cell_types.summary: Contracting heart muscle cells; standard monolayer protocols give a mixed but mostly ventricular-like, fetal-like population. Used for disease modelling, cardiotoxicity and drug screening, electrophysiology and engineered heart tissue.
cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 7-10; purity usually measured at day 15; ventricular-like electrophysiology and MLC2v expression increase over 30+ days.

morphology.endpoint: Sheets and thick strands of cells contracting in synchrony, with phase-bright ridges where the layer has piled up and flatter non-myocyte areas between them.

stages.label: Confluent hPSCs
stages.look: A fully confluent layer of small, tightly packed cells with a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio; no colony edges remain.

stages.label: Mesendoderm
stages.look: After the CHIR pulse the layer loosens and some cells float; survivors are small, uniform and migratory.

stages.label: Cardiac progenitors
stages.look: Dense multilayered sheet, darker and more textured, not yet beating.

stages.label: First beating
stages.look: Small twitching patches appear and spread into connected networks.

stages.label: Beating sheets
stages.look: Most of the well contracts as sheets and web-like strands.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Peaks about 24 h after CHIR; >90% expected in a good run.

markers.name: NKX2-5
markers.note: On from day 4-5 and maintained in working cardiomyocytes.

markers.name: TNNT2
markers.note: Standard purity readout; 80-98% reported at day 15.

markers.name: ACTN2
markers.note: Shows striated sarcomeres after replating as single cells.

markers.name: MYL7
markers.note: Present in all early hPSC-CMs; falls in ventricular cells with time.

markers.name: MYL2
markers.note: Ventricle-restricted; rises over weeks in culture.

markers.name: TNNI3
markers.note: Replaces the fetal isoform TNNI1 as cells mature.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Co-stain with cTnT; cTnT-negative SMA+ cells are non-myocytes (immature CMs can also be SMA+).

qc: >= 90% brachyury+ cells 24 h after CHIR99021 (Lian 2013)
Spontaneous beating by day 12 (Lian 2013); from about day 7 in CDM3 (Burridge 2014)
TNNT2+ >= 80% by flow at day 15
>95% TNNT2+ after lactate selection (Burridge 2014)

protocols.name: GiWi: Wnt on, then Wnt off (small molecules, RPMI/B27)
protocols.principle: A 24 h pulse of the GSK3 inhibitor CHIR99021 pushes a confluent hPSC monolayer into mesendoderm; blocking Wnt secretion with IWP2 two days later steers that mesoderm to a cardiac fate. No growth factors are needed.

source.authors: Lian X, Zhang J, Azarin SM, et al.
source.title: Directed cardiomyocyte differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells by modulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling under fully defined conditions.

protocols.efficiency: 80-98% cTnT+ cells after two weeks across the six hESC/iPSC lines tested
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs kept in mTeSR1 on hPSC-qualified Matrigel or Synthemax, passaged without enzymes (Versene). At day -4, singularise with Accutase and plate 0.5-1.5 million cells per well of a 12-well plate in mTeSR1 + 5 µM Y-27632; feed mTeSR1 daily on days -3 to -1 so the well is fully confluent on day 0.

stages.name: Mesendoderm induction (Wnt on)
stages.feeding: Single dose, removed after exactly 24 h
actions: Start only when the monolayer is fully confluent
Add 2 ml per 12-well of RPMI/B27-minus-insulin with CHIR99021 and write down the time
Change medium exactly 24 h later
stages.checkpoint: At 24 h at least 90% of cells should be brachyury (TBXT) positive by flow.

stages.name: Rest in basal medium
stages.feeding: One change on day 1, then leave for 48 h
actions: Replace with 2 ml fresh RPMI/B27-minus-insulin on day 1
Do not disturb until day 3

stages.name: Cardiac specification (Wnt off)
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + B-27 minus insulin (half conditioned, half fresh)
stages.feeding: Single dose at 72 h for 48 h
actions: At 72 h take 1 ml of the old medium from the well and mix with 1 ml fresh medium ('combined medium')
Add IWP2 to the combined medium, rock the plate to lift debris, aspirate the rest and add the 2 ml back
stages.checkpoint: NKX2-5 and ISL1 transcripts appear from day 4, protein from day 5.

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
actions: Replace with 2 ml RPMI/B27-minus-insulin

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte maintenance
actions: Switch to complete B-27 on day 7
Feed every 3 days; score beating areas
Quantify cTnT by flow at day 15
stages.checkpoint: cTnT detectable at day 8; first beating around day 8-10 and robust contraction by day 12.

tips: Titrate seeding density first (0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 million per 12-well) and keep the best one for that line.
The CHIR99021 optimum is line-dependent; the authors found 12 µM best for their six lines but recommend testing 6-14 µM.
Insulin is withheld until day 7 because it lowers yield during the early stages.
Cells can be kept beating in RPMI/B27 for months; metabolic (lactate) selection, as in Burridge 2014 or Tohyama 2013 (PMID 23168164), is commonly added afterwards to raise purity.
pitfalls: Sheet death or lifting after the CHIR pulse: density wrong, CHIR dose too high or left on too long.
No beating by day 12 / low cTnT at day 15: suboptimal density, or IWP2 dose or timing off; check brachyury at 24 h and NKX2-5 at day 5.
Timing matters: the 24 h CHIR and 72 h IWP2 time points should be kept to within an hour or two.

protocols.name: CDM3: chemically defined three-component medium
protocols.principle: Same Wnt on/off logic as GiWi, but B-27 is replaced by a medium of only RPMI 1640, recombinant human albumin and ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, with Wnt-C59 as the Wnt inhibitor. Glucose-free lactate medium then enriches the cardiomyocytes.

source.authors: Burridge PW, Matsa E, Shukla P, et al.
source.title: Chemically defined generation of human cardiomyocytes.

protocols.efficiency: 80-95% TNNT2+ by flow at day 15 across the hESC/hiPSC lines tested; >95% after lactate selection
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs adapted to E8 with EDTA passaging for at least 5 passages, on Synthemax II-SC, Matrigel (1:200) or, for long-term adhesion, laminin-521 / laminin-511 E8 fragment. Split 1:10-1:12 with 0.5 mM EDTA (2 µM thiazovivin for the first 24 h) and grow 4 days to about 85% confluence.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction (Wnt on)
stages.base_medium: CDM3 (RPMI 1640 + 500 µg/ml recombinant human albumin + 213 µg/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate)
actions: Switch from E8 to CDM3 + CHIR99021 at ~85% confluence
stages.checkpoint: POU5F1 falls and T/MIXL1 rise by day 2 (qPCR).

stages.name: Cardiac specification (Wnt off)
actions: Replace medium with CDM3 + Wnt-C59 on day 2

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte differentiation
actions: Change to plain CDM3 on day 4 and every other day
stages.checkpoint: Contracting cells from about day 7.

stages.name: Optional metabolic purification
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 without glucose + 500 µg/ml recombinant human albumin + 213 µg/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate

factors.name: Sodium DL-lactate
factors.role: Sole carbon source; non-cardiomyocytes die without glucose

stages.feeding: Change every 48 h (same schedule as CDM3)
actions: Replace CDM3 with the glucose-free lactate medium from day 10
Return to CDM3 after selection
stages.checkpoint: Purity rises from about 85% to >95% TNNT2+ after 6-10 days without glucose.

materials: Synthemax II-SC, Matrigel or laminin-521 / iMatrix-511
tips: Laminin-based matrices kept the beating sheets attached long term; on vitronectin peptide the sheets tended to peel off around day 15.
Yield reported as more than 3 x 10^5 cardiomyocytes per cm2.
B-27 contains galactose, so lactate selection has to be done in a B-27-free medium such as this one.
At day 15-20 action potentials look immature; ventricular-like cells predominate by day 30-35.
pitfalls: Ascorbic acid 2-phosphate is essential: without it the cells die.
Leaving out albumin does not kill the culture but sharply reduces yield.
The state of the starting hPSC culture drives efficiency; the authors required E8/EDTA adaptation before differentiating.

cell_types.notes: Efficiency depends strongly on the hPSC line, seeding density and CHIR99021 dose (12 µM for 24 h in RPMI/B27 versus 6 µM for 48 h in CDM3), so titrate both for each line. The product is an immature, mixed population (mostly ventricular-like with some atrial- and nodal-like cells); use the dedicated atrial or pacemaker protocols when subtype matters.

cell_types.name: Atrial cardiomyocytes
cell_types.summary: Working cardiomyocytes of the atria, with shorter action potentials and atrial-specific currents (IKur, IK,ACh). hPSC-derived atrial cells are used to model atrial fibrillation and to test atrial-selective drugs.
cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 8-10; atrial identity is usually assessed from day 20-30 and by electrophysiology later still.

morphology.endpoint: Beating sheets or EBs that look like standard hPSC-cardiomyocytes but usually contract faster; subtype cannot be judged by eye.

stages.label: hPSCs
stages.look: Near-confluent hPSC layer (monolayer route) or freshly formed aggregates (EB route).

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Loosened, migratory small cells after Wnt activation.

stages.label: Cardiac mesoderm under retinoic acid
stages.look: Dense multilayered sheet, not yet beating.

stages.label: First beating
stages.look: Twitching patches merge into networks.

stages.label: Atrial-like cardiomyocytes
stages.look: Rapidly beating sheets; smaller cells than ventricular cultures after replating.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: ALDH1A2
markers.note: Marks the mesoderm that gives atrial cells (Lee 2017).

markers.name: NR2F2
markers.note: Induced by retinoic acid; strongly enriched over ventricular cultures.

markers.name: MYL7
markers.note: Stays high in atrial cells while MLC2v stays off.

markers.name: KCNA5
markers.note: Carries IKur; functional test with a selective blocker.

markers.name: IRX4
markers.note: Ventricular transcription factor; should be down.

functional_assays: IKur and IK,ACh currents / response to carbachol
qc: cTnT+ around 87-90% at day 20 (Cyganek 2018)
Predominantly MLC2a+/MLC2v- cardiomyocytes in long-term culture (Cyganek 2018)
NR2F1/NR2F2 up and MYL2/IRX4 down versus a no-retinoic-acid control (Devalla 2015)

protocols.name: Monolayer Wnt on/off plus retinoic acid on days 3-6
protocols.principle: A standard CHIR99021 then IWP2 monolayer differentiation in albumin/ascorbate RPMI; adding 1 µM retinoic acid during cardiac mesoderm specification redirects the cells from a ventricular to an atrial fate.

source.authors: Cyganek L, Tiburcy M, Sekeres K, et al.
source.title: Deep phenotyping of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes.

protocols.efficiency: About 87-90% cTnT+ at day 20; in RA-treated cultures about 95% of cardiomyocytes were MLC2a+/MLC2v- at around day 100 (versus about 11% in controls)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs on Geltrex-coated plates grown to 80-90% confluence.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction (Wnt on)
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 with GlutaMAX and HEPES + 0.5 mg/ml recombinant human albumin + 0.2 mg/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate
actions: Start at 80-90% confluence

stages.name: Cardiac specification (Wnt off) with atrial patterning
stages.feeding: IWP2 for 48 h; retinoic acid added from day 3
actions: Add IWP2 on day 2
Begin retinoic acid on day 3

stages.name: Retinoic acid continued
actions: Remove IWP2; keep retinoic acid until day 6

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte differentiation
actions: Continue in differentiation medium without factors

stages.name: Maintenance
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 with GlutaMAX and HEPES + 2% B-27
actions: Switch to B-27 medium from day 8
Replate around day 15
stages.checkpoint: Beating monolayers.

stages.name: Metabolic selection
stages.base_medium: Glucose-free RPMI 1640 + 0.5 mg/ml albumin + 0.2 mg/ml ascorbate
actions: Apply after replating
Return to B-27 medium afterwards

tips: Run a no-retinoic-acid well in parallel: it gives the matched ventricular control used throughout the paper.
Retinoic acid is light-sensitive; make fresh dilutions and protect from light.
Subtype identity (MLC2a versus MLC2v) sharpens with long culture; the paper's subtype percentages are from about day 100.
pitfalls: Retinoic acid dose and window matter: later papers report that the atrial action-potential phenotype depends on the RA concentration, so do not assume 1 µM on days 3-6 transfers unchanged to every line.
MLC2a alone is not proof of atrial identity in young cultures because all early hPSC-CMs express it; confirm with NR2F2, KCNA5, NPPA or electrophysiology.
unverified: Day labels for the CHIR99021 (0-2) and IWP2 (2-4) steps are inferred from the stated consecutive 48 h treatments; the Methods as read gave durations, not day numbers.
Medium-change frequency and the exact replating day before lactate selection were not captured.
Whether the day-8 B-27 is the insulin-containing formulation is not stated explicitly in the text read.

protocols.name: Spin embryoid bodies with retinoic acid from day 4
protocols.principle: Growth-factor-induced cardiac mesoderm in spin EBs (BPEL medium) is exposed to 1 µM retinoic acid on days 4-7, which induces COUP-TFI/II and an atrial gene and ion-channel programme.

source.authors: Devalla HD, Schwach V, Ford JW, et al.
source.title: Atrial-like cardiomyocytes from human pluripotent stem cells are a robust preclinical model for assessing atrial-selective pharmacology.

protocols.efficiency: About 50% NKX2-5-GFP+ cells with retinoic acid versus about 65% in the untreated control
protocols.start_requirements: NKX2-5-eGFP reporter hESCs maintained on irradiated mouse embryonic fibroblasts; harvested and aggregated as spin EBs on day 0.

stages.name: Spin EB formation and mesoderm induction
actions: Resuspend harvested hESCs in BPEL with the factors and spin into aggregates

stages.name: Refresh
actions: Replace with plain BPEL

stages.name: Atrial specification
stages.feeding: Added on day 4; refreshed with plain BPEL on day 7
actions: Add retinoic acid on day 4
Change to BPEL on day 7
stages.checkpoint: COUP-TFI/II transcripts rise within 24 h of retinoic acid.

stages.name: Maturation
stages.feeding: Not stated in the text read
actions: Transfer EBs to gelatin-coated dishes on day 7
Dissociate with TrypLE Select around day 17 for electrophysiology
stages.checkpoint: Beating EBs; atrial-like action potentials when patched 10-14 days after dissociation.

tips: The no-retinoic-acid arm of the same protocol gives ventricular-like cells for comparison.
Atrial readouts used: NR2F1/NR2F2 (COUP-TFI/II), KCNA5, KCNJ3, SLN, NPPA and PITX2 up; MYL2, IRX4, HEY2 and HAND1 down.
pitfalls: Retinoic acid lowers the fraction of NKX2-5+ cells, so total cardiomyocyte yield is below that of the control arm.
The published work used hESCs on feeders and a reporter line; expect to re-optimise growth-factor doses (given as 20-30 ng/ml ranges) for feeder-free iPSCs.
unverified: EB size (cells per aggregate) and feeding schedule after day 7 were not captured from the text read.

protocols.name: Keller/Protze-lab EB protocol: atrial mesoderm plus retinoic acid on days 3-5
protocols.principle: Atrial cardiomyocytes arise from a different mesoderm than ventricular ones: mesoderm is induced with lower BMP4 and Activin A than for the ventricular fate, then retinoic acid is given together with the Wnt inhibitor on days 3-5.

source.authors: Lim AA, Pouyabahar D, Ashraf M, et al.
source.title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals CD34 as a marker of human sinoatrial node pacemaker cardiomyocytes.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs at about 80% confluence, dissociated to single cells with TrypLE. EBs are kept in suspension on poly-HEMA-coated dishes under 5% O2 until day 11, then ambient oxygen.

stages.name: EB formation
stages.base_medium: Base medium (StemPro-34 with 2 mM L-glutamine, 50 µg/ml ascorbic acid, 75 µg/ml transferrin, 50 µg/ml monothioglycerol) used at 20% in IMDM, + 0.01x ITS-X
stages.feeding: 18 h on an orbital shaker (80 rpm)
actions: Suspend single cells at 1 x 10^6 cells/ml in low-attachment 6 cm dishes
Culture at 5% O2
stages.checkpoint: Small uniform aggregates after 18 h.

stages.name: Atrial mesoderm induction

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: Mesoderm inducer (lower than the 10 ng/ml used for ventricular mesoderm)

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: Mesoderm patterning (lower than the 8 ng/ml used for ventricular mesoderm)

actions: Move EBs into mesoderm induction medium on day 1

stages.name: Cardiac induction with atrial patterning
actions: Wash EBs once with IMDM before changing medium on day 3

stages.name: Maintenance
actions: Move to ambient oxygen on day 11
Analyse around day 25 (SIRPA+ CD90- cardiomyocytes)
stages.checkpoint: Beating EBs.

tips: The concept and original protocol are from Lee JH et al. 2017 Cell Stem Cell (PMID 28777944, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2017.07.003): atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes derive from distinct mesoderm populations distinguishable by RALDH2 and CD235a.
The matched ventricular arm uses 10 ng/ml BMP4 and 8 ng/ml Activin A on days 1-3 and no retinoic acid.
BMP4 and Activin A doses for mesoderm induction are line-dependent in this system and are normally titrated per line.
pitfalls: Needs a hypoxia incubator and an orbital shaker; more hands-on than monolayer methods.
Giving retinoic acid to the wrong (ventricular-type) mesoderm does not produce good atrial cells; the mesoderm induction doses matter as much as the retinoic acid.
unverified: Concentrations and timings are the current version of the protocol as written in Lim et al. 2024 (same laboratory), who state it follows their earlier protocols 'with modifications'; the Methods of Lee et al. 2017 itself could not be accessed, so differences from the original are not documented here.
No efficiency figure for the atrial arm was captured.

cell_types.notes: Always differentiate a no-retinoic-acid control alongside; atrial identity is defined relative to it. Retinoic acid dose and window differ between protocols (1 µM on days 3-6 in monolayer, 1 µM on days 4-7 in spin EBs, 0.5 µM on days 3-5 in the Toronto EB system) and are line-dependent.

cell_types.name: Sinoatrial node pacemaker cells
cell_types.summary: Specialised, NKX2-5-negative cardiomyocytes of the sinoatrial node that fire spontaneously and set heart rate. hPSC-derived versions are used to study automaticity and sinus node disease and as candidate biological pacemakers.
route: Posterior cardiac mesoderm (BMP + retinoic acid, FGF/TGF-beta off)
cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 10; pacemaker identity and sorting are usually assessed at day 19-25.

morphology.endpoint: Small, fast and regularly beating clusters or EBs; cells are smaller and less striated than working cardiomyocytes, but identity needs markers or electrophysiology.

stages.label: hPSCs / fresh aggregates
stages.look: Near-confluent hPSCs (monolayer) or single cells aggregating overnight (EB route).

stages.label: Embryoid bodies
stages.look: Small smooth aggregates in suspension.

stages.label: Cardiac mesoderm under patterning
stages.look: EBs enlarge slightly; no beating yet.

stages.label: First beating
stages.look: EBs or patches begin contracting, faster than ventricular controls.

stages.label: Pacemaker-like cardiomyocytes
stages.look: Rhythmic, rapidly beating EBs or clusters.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: TNNT2
markers.note: Total cardiomyocyte content (60-90% in the monolayer protocol).

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Reported surface marker for sorting SAN-like cells within SIRPA+ CD90- cardiomyocytes (Lim 2024).

markers.name: NKX2-5
markers.note: Should be low or absent in pacemaker cells.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Side population when Wnt inhibition is insufficient.

functional_assays: Spontaneous beating rate (faster than working cardiomyocytes)
Patch-clamp: pacemaker action potentials with diastolic depolarisation, funny current (If)
Rate response to ivabradine and to adrenergic/cholinergic agonists
Pacing of co-cultured ventricular monolayers or tissue
qc: Contraction from about day 10 with faster beating than the ventricular control (Wiesinger 2022)
SHOX2, TBX3, ISL1, HCN4 up and NKX2-5 down versus the control arm
NKX2-5-negative, CD34+ fraction within SIRPA+ CD90- cardiomyocytes at day 25 (Lim 2024)

protocols.name: Protze-lab EB protocol: BMP4 + retinoic acid with TGF-beta and FGF inhibition
protocols.principle: Low-dose mesoderm induction followed, at the cardiac mesoderm stage, by BMP4 and retinoic acid while Activin/TGF-beta and FGF signalling are blocked; this yields NKX2-5-negative sinoatrial-node-like pacemaker cardiomyocytes instead of working myocardium.

source.authors: Lim AA, Pouyabahar D, Ashraf M, et al.
source.title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals CD34 as a marker of human sinoatrial node pacemaker cardiomyocytes.

protocols.efficiency: Mixed cultures of NKX2-5-negative pacemaker-like and NKX2-5+ cardiomyocytes; CD34 marks the pacemaker fraction (about 54% of NKX2-5-negative cardiomyocytes were CD34+ at day 25) and CD34 sorting enriches them
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs at about 80% confluence, dissociated to single cells with TrypLE. EBs in suspension on poly-HEMA-coated dishes at 5% O2 until day 11, then ambient oxygen.

stages.name: EB formation
stages.base_medium: Base medium (StemPro-34 with 2 mM L-glutamine, 50 µg/ml ascorbic acid, 75 µg/ml transferrin, 50 µg/ml monothioglycerol) used at 20% in IMDM, + 0.01x ITS-X
stages.feeding: 18 h on an orbital shaker (80 rpm)
actions: Suspend at 1 x 10^6 cells/ml in low-attachment 6 cm dishes
Culture at 5% O2

stages.name: Pacemaker mesoderm induction
actions: Move EBs into induction medium on day 1

stages.name: Pacemaker specification

factors.name: PD173074
factors.conc: 500-1000 nM, added on day 3 or day 4 depending on line
factors.role: FGF receptor inhibitor; suppresses NKX2-5+ working myocardium

stages.feeding: Single addition on day 3 (PD173074 on day 3 for HES3-NKX2-5-eGFP, day 4 for HES2)
actions: Wash EBs once with IMDM, then add specification medium

stages.name: Recovery
actions: Change medium on day 6

stages.name: Maintenance
actions: Move to ambient oxygen on day 11
Analyse or sort around day 25: SIRPA+ CD90- cardiomyocytes, NKX2-5-negative, CD34+
stages.checkpoint: Fast, regularly beating EBs.

tips: Original protocol: Protze SI et al. 2017 Nat Biotechnol (PMID 27941801, doi 10.1038/nbt.3745).
An NKX2-5 reporter line makes it easy to follow the NKX2-5-negative pacemaker fraction; without one, sort SIRPA+ CD90- CD34+ cells.
PD173074 dose and day of addition are line-specific in the authors' hands.
pitfalls: Unsorted cultures still contain NKX2-5+ atrial-like cardiomyocytes and non-myocytes; do not treat them as pure pacemaker cells.
Mesoderm induction doses (BMP4/Activin A) normally need titration for each line in this EB system.
unverified: Values are those written in Lim et al. 2024 (same laboratory, 'previously reported protocols with modifications'); the Methods of Protze et al. 2017 could not be accessed, so the original 2017 concentrations are not confirmed here.
Overall percentage of pacemaker-like cells per culture was not captured as a single figure.

protocols.name: Monolayer SAN protocol (BPEL; BMP4, retinoic acid, Wnt/TGF-beta/FGF inhibition on days 4-6)
protocols.principle: A growth-factor monolayer cardiac differentiation in BPEL in which, on days 4-6, cardiac mesoderm receives low BMP4 and retinoic acid while Wnt, ALK5 and FGF receptor signalling are inhibited, giving sinoatrial-like cardiomyocytes; XAV939 alone for 96 h gives the ventricular-like control.

source.authors: Wiesinger A, Li J, Fokkert L, et al.
source.title: A single cell transcriptional roadmap of human pacemaker cell differentiation.

protocols.efficiency: 60-90% TNNT2+ cells at day 19 (same range for the pacemaker and ventricular arms)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in mTeSR1 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel; seed at 2.5-3 x 10^4 cells/cm2 and start when 80-90% confluent.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Replace mTeSR1 with BPEL plus factors at 80-90% confluence

stages.name: Wnt inhibition
actions: Replace with BPEL + XAV939

stages.name: Pacemaker specification

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: Wnt inhibition (required to keep cells myocardial rather than proepicardial)

actions: Add the five-factor cocktail on day 4

stages.name: Maturation
actions: Replace with plain BPEL on day 6
Analyse at day 19
stages.checkpoint: Contraction from about day 10; pacemaker wells beat visibly faster than ventricular control wells.

tips: Ventricular control: BPEL + 5 µM XAV939 from day 3 for 96 h, then BPEL.
Readouts used: SHOX2, TBX3, ISL1, HCN4 up and NKX2-5, MYL2 down versus the ventricular arm.
pitfalls: Leaving out the Wnt inhibitor during days 4-6 collapses the cardiomyocyte fraction (about 10% TNNT2+) and gives proepicardial-like (WT1+, PDPN+) cells instead.
The culture is a mix of sinoatrial head, tail and transition-zone-like cells plus a proepicardial side population (about 10% PDPN+).

protocols.name: GiWi followed by a second Wnt pulse on days 5-7
protocols.principle: After a standard GiWi cardiac induction, canonical Wnt is switched back on (CHIR99021 or recombinant WNT5B) at the cardiac progenitor stage, which diverts progenitors toward pacemaker-like cardiomyocytes.

source.authors: Ren J, Han P, Ma X, et al.
source.title: Canonical Wnt5b Signaling Directs Outlying Nkx2.5+ Mesoderm into Pacemaker Cardiomyocytes.

protocols.start_requirements: hESCs (TNNT2-GFP reporter H9 in the paper) in E8 on Geltrex, expanded to 80% confluence.

stages.name: Mesendoderm induction
actions: Start at 80% confluence

stages.name: Rest
actions: Remove CHIR after 24 h

stages.name: Cardiac specification
actions: Add IWP2 on day 3

stages.name: Pacemaker induction (Wnt back on)

factors.name: WNT5B (alternative to CHIR)
factors.role: Recombinant ligand used instead of CHIR

actions: Replace medium with CHIR99021 (or WNT5B); use DMSO for the control cardiomyocyte arm

stages.name: Maintenance
stages.feeding: Not stated in the text read
actions: Analyse or sort cardiomyocytes at day 15
stages.checkpoint: Beating cultures.

tips: Simple add-on to an existing GiWi workflow; compare against a DMSO-treated arm from the same plate.
pitfalls: The human experiments read here used a single TNNT2 reporter hESC line; confirm pacemaker identity (SHOX2, TBX3, HCN4 up; NKX2-5 down) and beating rate in your own line.
unverified: Efficiency (fraction of pacemaker-like cells) was not captured.
Feeding interval after day 7 not captured.

cell_types.notes: No protocol gives pure pacemaker cells: cultures contain atrial-like cardiomyocytes, transition-zone cells and proepicardial or other non-myocytes, so plan for a reporter line or surface-marker sorting. Dosing of BMP4, retinoic acid and the FGF inhibitor is line-dependent.

cell_types.name: Epicardial cells
cell_types.summary: The mesothelial sheet covering the heart; in development it gives rise to cardiac fibroblasts and coronary smooth muscle and signals to the myocardium. hPSC-derived epicardium is used to study EMT, to make epicardium-derived fibroblasts and smooth muscle, and as a supportive cell type in engineered heart tissue.
cell_types.maturation_note: WT1+ pro-epicardial cells by day 12-15; ALDH1A2 and tight junctions (ZO-1) appear a few days later.

morphology.endpoint: A flat cobblestone epithelium of polygonal cells with clear borders; cells turn spindle-shaped if TGF-beta signalling is not blocked during expansion.

stages.label: hPSCs
stages.look: Confluent or near-confluent hPSC layer.

stages.label: Mesendoderm
stages.look: Small, loosened, uniform cells after the first CHIR pulse.

stages.label: Cardiac progenitors
stages.look: Dense sheet; cells are dissociated and replated sparsely at this point.

stages.label: Emerging epithelium
stages.look: Islands of polygonal cells appear during the second Wnt pulse.

stages.label: Pro-epicardial sheet
stages.look: Confluent cobblestone monolayer.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: >90% at 24 h in the Bao protocol.

markers.name: ALDH1A2
markers.note: Retinoic-acid-synthesising epicardium; comes up after day 12.

markers.name: TJP1
markers.note: Continuous junctional staining in a proper epithelium.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Rises if cells undergo spontaneous EMT.

functional_assays: EMT in response to TGFB1 or bFGF
Differentiation into smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts
qc: >90% brachyury+ at 24 h and about 50% NKX2-5+/ISL1+ at day 6 (Bao 2017)
>90% WT1+ at day 12 (Bao 2017)
<1% cTnT+ cells (Bao 2017)

protocols.name: GiWi cardiac progenitors, then a second CHIR99021 pulse (defined, xeno-free)
protocols.principle: Cardiac progenitors made by Wnt activation then inhibition are replated at low density on day 6 and given CHIR99021 again for two days; reactivating Wnt at this stage turns NKX2-5+/ISL1+ progenitors into WT1+ epicardial cells instead of cardiomyocytes. TGF-beta inhibition then allows long-term expansion.

source.authors: Bao X, Lian X, Qian T, et al.
source.title: Directed differentiation and long-term maintenance of epicardial cells derived from human pluripotent stem cells under fully defined conditions.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs (>95% OCT4+) in mTeSR1 or E8 on Matrigel or Synthemax. At day -3 plate 0.5-2.0 million singularised cells per well of a 12-well plate with ROCK inhibitor and feed daily. For E8-grown cells, pre-condition with 0.1-0.6 µM CHIR99021 on day -1.

stages.name: Mesendoderm induction
actions: Add 2 ml per 12-well and note the time
Change medium at 24 h
stages.checkpoint: >90% brachyury+ at 24 h.

stages.name: Rest
actions: Replace with fresh basal medium

stages.name: Cardiac progenitor specification
stages.base_medium: RPMI basal medium (half conditioned, half fresh)
actions: Mix 1 ml old medium with 1 ml fresh, add IWP2 and return to the well

stages.name: Progenitor rest
actions: Replace with fresh basal medium
stages.checkpoint: By day 6 about half the cells are NKX2-5+ and ISL1+ (flow); below 20% progenitors gives a poor epicardial yield.

stages.name: Replating
stages.base_medium: LaSR basal (Advanced DMEM/F12 + 2.5 mM GlutaMAX + 100 µg/ml ascorbic acid) or RPMI/Vc/Ins (RPMI + 100 µg/ml ascorbic acid + 1 µg/ml insulin)
actions: Dissociate with Accutase for 5 min
Seed on gelatin- or Synthemax-coated plates at 20,000-40,000 cells/cm2 in LaSR basal (or 40,000-80,000 cells/cm2 in RPMI/Vc/Ins)

stages.name: Epicardial induction (Wnt on again)
stages.feeding: Fresh CHIR medium on day 7 and day 8
actions: Feed 1 ml per 12-well with CHIR99021 on both days
stages.checkpoint: Cobblestone morphology visible from day 8.

stages.name: Pro-epicardial maturation
actions: Feed daily without factors on days 9, 10 and 11
Harvest, freeze or passage on day 12
stages.checkpoint: >90% WT1+ at day 12; WT1 detectable from day 10. ALDH1A2 and ZO-1 come up by about day 16.

tips: Day 5 or day 7 progenitors also work if CHIR99021 is given for the following 2 days.

For expansion, passage confluent cells 1:3 to 1:9 and keep them in LaSR basal or RPMI/Vc/Ins with 0.5 µM A83-01 or 2 µM SB431542; without a TGF-beta inhibitor they undergo EMT into smooth-muscle-like cells within 2-3 passages.
Use Accutase for the day-12 passage; Versene worked better for the authors after about 8 passages.
The same paper gives short add-on steps to turn the epicardial cells into fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells.
pitfalls: Low WT1 at day 12 usually traces back to too few NKX2-5+/ISL1+ progenitors on day 6, wrong replating density, or a CHIR99021 dose that needs re-titrating.
If day-6 cells are left unreplated and untreated they become beating cardiomyocytes.
unverified: Exact composition of the 'RPMI basal medium' used on days 0-6 (the albumin-free GiWi2 variant) was not captured from the text read; the original GiWi version uses RPMI/B27 minus insulin.

protocols.name: EB mesoderm, then BMP4 + Wnt activation on days 4-6
protocols.principle: KDR+PDGFRA+ cardiovascular mesoderm is made in embryoid bodies, then plated as a monolayer; BMP4 together with active Wnt signalling (CHIR99021) specifies WT1+ pro-epicardium, whereas BMP4 with Wnt inhibition gives cardiomyocytes.

source.authors: Witty AD, Mihic A, Tam RY, et al.
source.title: Generation of the epicardial lineage from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: About 87% WT1+ at day 15 by immunostaining, rising to >90% eight days after passage
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs maintained on irradiated MEFs and feeder-depleted on Matrigel for 2 days before dissociation into EBs.

stages.name: EB formation
actions: Dissociate hESCs and aggregate into EBs

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: On day 4 (day 3 for the iPSC line used) dissociate EBs with TrypLE
stages.checkpoint: KDR+PDGFRA+ mesoderm at day 4-5.

stages.name: Pro-epicardial specification

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: Required for both epicardial and cardiomyocyte fates

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: Wnt activation; selects epicardial over cardiomyocyte fate

actions: Plate the dissociated cells on gelatin-coated plates at 1 x 10^5 cells per well
Add BMP4 and CHIR99021

stages.name: Epicardial maturation
actions: Maintain to day 15
For passage, lift the sheet with collagenase B, dissociate with TrypLE and replate on Matrigel with ROCK inhibitor
stages.checkpoint: Cobblestone WT1+ epithelium at day 15.

tips: EMT of the passaged epicardial cells was induced with TGFB1 and/or bFGF, giving smooth-muscle-like and fibroblast-like derivatives.
The matched cardiomyocyte condition is BMP4 plus a Wnt inhibitor (XAV939 or IWP2) in the same day 4-6 window.
pitfalls: Adding bFGF during days 4-6 suppresses WT1; blocking BMP (dorsomorphin) gives neither epicardium nor cardiomyocytes.
Feeder-dependent hESC starting cultures; growth factor doses for mesoderm induction need titration for other lines.
unverified: CHIR99021 concentration for days 4-6 is given in the figures, not in the text read; set to null.
Whether SB-431542 (5.4 µM) and VEGF (5 ng/ml), which are in the paper's default day 4-6 medium, are kept in the BMP4 + CHIR epicardial condition was not confirmed.
Well format for the 1 x 10^5 cells per well plating was not captured.

protocols.name: Lateral plate mesoderm, then WNT3A + BMP4 + retinoic acid (chemically defined)
protocols.principle: hPSCs are taken through early mesoderm to lateral plate mesoderm with FGF2 and high BMP4, then plated sparsely in WNT3A, BMP4 and retinoic acid for 10 days to give an epicardial epithelium that can be pushed on to smooth muscle cells or fibroblasts.

source.authors: Iyer D, Gambardella L, Bernard WG, et al.
source.title: Robust derivation of epicardium and its differentiated smooth muscle cell progeny from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on gelatin-coated plates in chemically defined medium (CDM-BSA) with Activin A (10 ng/ml) and FGF2 (12 ng/ml).

stages.name: Early mesoderm

factors.name: LY294002
factors.role: PI3K inhibitor; promotes exit from pluripotency

actions: Switch from maintenance medium to CDM-PVA with FGF2, LY294002 and BMP4

stages.name: Lateral plate mesoderm
actions: Change to FGF2 + high BMP4
stages.checkpoint: Most cells ISL1+ (over 90%) and many NKX2-5+; over 60% KDR+.

stages.name: Epicardial differentiation
actions: Replate lateral plate mesoderm at 2.5 x 10^3 cells/cm2 (as written in the paper)
Culture in WNT3A + BMP4 + retinoic acid
stages.checkpoint: Cobblestone epithelium expressing WT1, TBX18 and TCF21.

materials: CDM-PVA (IMDM/F12 1:1, PVA 1 mg/ml, lipids, transferrin, insulin, monothioglycerol)
tips: Epicardium-derived smooth muscle: PDGF-BB 10 ng/ml + TGFB1 2 ng/ml in CDM-PVA for 12 days; fibroblast-like cells: VEGF 50 ng/ml + FGF2 50 ng/ml for 12 days.
Retinoic acid at 4 µM was chosen because 6 µM increased cell death after 3-4 days.
pitfalls: The authors report that endogenous Wnt signalling is sufficient but not optimal for epicardial differentiation, which is why WNT3A is included.
The very low replating density is important for forming an epithelial sheet; check it against the paper before scaling.
unverified: No single efficiency figure (% WT1+) was captured.
Medium-change interval during the 10-day epicardial step was not captured.

cell_types.notes: Epicardial cells drift into mesenchyme (EMT) unless a TGF-beta receptor inhibitor is kept in the expansion medium. The three protocols start from different mesoderm (cardiac progenitors versus lateral plate) and use different inducers, so do not mix steps between them.

cell_types.name: Cardiac fibroblasts
cell_types.summary: The matrix-producing stromal cells of the heart, mostly of epicardial origin. hPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts are used to model fibrosis and myofibroblast activation and as the stromal component of engineered heart tissue and cardiac microtissues.
cell_types.maturation_note: Fibroblast morphology by day 18-20; cells are expandable for several passages and activate to myofibroblasts with TGFB1 or serum.

morphology.endpoint: Elongated spindle-shaped cells growing in swirls and parallel bundles; activated myofibroblasts are larger and flatter with visible stress fibres.

stages.label: hPSCs
stages.look: Confluent hPSC layer.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Small loosened cells after CHIR99021.

stages.label: Cardiac progenitors
stages.look: Dense sheet, non-beating.

stages.label: Epicardial intermediate (epicardial route)
stages.look: Cobblestone epithelium; skipped in the GiFGF route, where cells become mesenchymal directly.

stages.label: Cardiac fibroblasts
stages.look: Spindle cells in aligned swirls.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: High at day 12 in the epicardial route, then falls in fibroblasts.

markers.name: DDR2
markers.note: Collagen receptor used as a fibroblast marker.

markers.name: POSTN
markers.note: Fibroblast matrix protein; rises with activation.

markers.name: GATA4
markers.note: Cardiac-specific transcription factor that separates cardiac from dermal fibroblasts.

markers.name: TBX20
markers.note: Cardiac identity marker retained in cardiac fibroblasts.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Should be low in quiescent cells; rises with TGFB1.

qc: >90% COL1+, DDR2+ and TCF21+ by flow (Zhang H 2019)
80-90% TE-7+ at early passage (Zhang J 2019)
Low alpha-SMA in maintenance medium, inducible with TGFB1

protocols.name: GiFGF: CHIR99021 then high-dose bFGF (second heart field route)
protocols.principle: After a one-day CHIR99021 pulse, cardiac mesoderm is switched on day 2 into a defined fibroblast medium with 75 ng/ml bFGF instead of a Wnt inhibitor; FGF signalling drives the progenitors through a second-heart-field-like state to cardiac fibroblasts and prevents cardiomyocyte formation.

source.authors: Zhang J, Tao R, Campbell KF, et al.
source.title: Functional cardiac fibroblasts derived from human pluripotent stem cells via second heart field progenitors.

protocols.efficiency: 80-90% of cells positive for the fibroblast antigen TE-7 at early passage, rising to about 99% with further passaging
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated with Versene and seeded on Matrigel-coated 6-well plates at 1.5-2.0 x 10^6 cells per well in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632; fed daily for 5-6 days until 100% confluent.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Add 2.5 ml per 6-well at 100% confluence

stages.name: Rest
actions: Replace with 2.5 ml fresh medium

stages.name: Fibroblast specification and expansion
stages.base_medium: Cardiac fibroblast basal medium (CFBM, defined; formulation in the paper's supplementary table)
actions: Change to CFBM + bFGF after day 2 and before day 3
Feed every other day until day 20
stages.checkpoint: No beating cells should appear; spindle cells take over the well.

tips: From day 20, passage with 0.05% trypsin-EDTA into uncoated plastic 6-well plates at 300,000 cells per well in FibroGRO + 2% FBS; feed every other day and split every 4-6 days (5,800 cells/cm2).
Starting bFGF on day 2 was the best window; day 3 or 4 with high bFGF caused extensive cell death after day 6.
pitfalls: Cells activate into alpha-SMA-high myofibroblasts in serum-rich medium (DMEM + 10% FBS) or with TGFB1; keep them in the fibroblast medium for a quiescent phenotype.
TE-7 positivity declines again as the cells approach senescence at high passage.
unverified: CFBM composition is in a supplementary table that was not read; obtain it from the paper before starting.

protocols.name: Epicardial route: cardiac progenitors, epicardial cells, then FGF2 + SB431542
protocols.principle: Cardiac progenitors (CHIR99021 then IWR-1) are replated and converted to epicardial cells with CHIR99021 and retinoic acid, then differentiated into quiescent cardiac fibroblasts in fibroblast growth medium with FGF2 while TGF-beta signalling is blocked to prevent myofibroblast activation.

source.authors: Zhang H, Shen M, Wu JC
source.title: Generation of Quiescent Cardiac Fibroblasts Derived from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.

protocols.efficiency: >90% of cells positive for COL1, DDR2 and TCF21 by flow at day 18 (original Circ Res report)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in E8 on Matrigel-coated 6-well plates, 80-90% confluent on day 0.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Add 3 ml per 6-well

stages.name: Rest
actions: Replace medium

stages.name: Cardiac progenitor specification
actions: Add IWR-1 medium on day 3

stages.name: Progenitor rest
actions: Replace medium

stages.name: Pro-epicardial induction
stages.feeding: Replate on day 6; fresh CHIR + retinoic acid on day 7
actions: Dissociate with Accutase and seed at 20,000 cells/cm2 (about 1:12)
On day 7 change to medium with CHIR99021 and retinoic acid only

stages.name: Epicardial expansion
stages.feeding: Plain medium on day 9; from day 12 every other day with SB431542
actions: On day 11 passage 1:3 to 1:6 into medium with SB431542
stages.checkpoint: Cobblestone epicardial sheet; >90% WT1+ expected at day 12.

stages.name: Fibroblast differentiation
stages.feeding: Change on day 16; replate on day 18; then every other day
actions: Day 14: seed epicardial cells on Matrigel at 10,000 cells/cm2 (about 1:3)
Day 18: passage again at 10,000 cells/cm2
stages.checkpoint: Spindle-shaped fibroblasts by day 18.

tips: First described in Zhang H et al. 2019 Circ Res (PMID 31288631, doi 10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.119.315491); the step-by-step values here are from the same group's protocol chapter.
The first 6 days are the same as for cardiomyocytes; replating density on day 6 decides between epicardial cells (sparse) and beating cardiomyocytes (left in place).
With SB431542 in the medium most cells stay quiescent (about 5% alpha-SMA+) up to passage 5; remove the inhibitor at least a day before TGF-beta activation experiments.
pitfalls: Massive death or detachment by day 2 means the CHIR99021 dose or duration needs titrating for that line.
Without the TGF-beta inhibitor the fibroblasts spontaneously become myofibroblasts in culture.
unverified: The Circ Res paper's own Methods are in an online supplement that was not read; small differences from the chapter (the paper describes six days in fibroblast medium to day 18) are possible.

cell_types.notes: Fibroblast markers are not specific on their own; confirm cardiac identity with GATA4/TBX20 and absence of cTnT and CD31. Cells activate easily on stiff plastic and in serum, so decide up front whether you need quiescent or activated cells and choose the maintenance medium accordingly.

cell_types.name: Endothelial cells
cell_types.summary: The cells lining blood vessels. hPSC-derived endothelial cells are used for vascular disease modelling, barrier and inflammation assays, angiogenesis assays and to vascularise organoids and engineered tissues.
cell_types.maturation_note: CD144+/CD34+ cells by day 5-6; sorted cells mature and expand over a further 1-2 weeks but lose proliferative capacity with passage.

morphology.endpoint: After sorting, a cobblestone monolayer of polygonal cells that become elongated when sparse; unsorted day-6 cultures show endothelial islands among mesenchymal cells.

stages.label: Sparse hPSCs
stages.look: Single cells and small clusters after single-cell plating.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Cells spread, flatten and proliferate into a loose sheet.

stages.label: Vascular mesoderm
stages.look: Confluent, heterogeneous sheet with debris; medium acidifies.

stages.label: Endothelial islands
stages.look: Patches of cobblestone cells among spindle-shaped mural cells.

stages.label: Purified endothelium
stages.look: Uniform cobblestone monolayer after CD144 or CD34 selection.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: KDR
markers.note: Vascular-competent mesoderm; stays on in endothelium.

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Used for day-5 selection; lost with maturation in the Lian protocol.

qc: CD144+ 62-89% before sorting and about 96% after MACS (Patsch 2015)
>50% CD34+CD31+ at day 5 (Lian 2014)
CD43/CD45 negative

protocols.name: CHIR99021 + BMP4 mesoderm, then VEGF + forskolin (6 days)
protocols.principle: GSK3 inhibition plus BMP4 converts a sparse hPSC monolayer to lateral mesoderm in three days; a short exposure to high VEGF-A with forskolin (cAMP/PKA activation) then drives endothelial commitment, and CD144+ cells are purified magnetically on day 6.

source.authors: Patsch C, Challet-Meylan L, Thoma EC, et al.
source.title: Generation of vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: 62-89% CD144+ cells before sorting; about 96% after CD144 MACS
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in mTeSR1 on Matrigel, passaged with Accutase. Day 0: seed single cells at 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632.

stages.name: Plating
actions: Seed 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2
Optimise density per line
stages.checkpoint: Evenly spread, sub-confluent cells on day 1.

stages.name: Lateral mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal 1:1 with N2, B27 minus vitamin A and beta-mercaptoethanol)
stages.feeding: Three days with no medium change
actions: Use a generous volume (3 ml per 12-well)
Do not change medium for 3 days
stages.checkpoint: Medium turns light yellow by day 4; some floating dead cells are normal.

stages.name: Endothelial induction
actions: Feed 2 ml per 12-well daily
On day 6 dissociate with Accutase and isolate CD144+ cells with magnetic beads (or FACS)
Replate sorted cells on fibronectin in StemPro-34 + 50 ng/ml VEGF-A
stages.checkpoint: Up to 80% CD144+ by flow on day 6.

tips: Expansion: fibronectin-coated flasks (about 2 µg/cm2), StemPro-34 + 50 ng/ml VEGF-A.
The same day 1-4 mesoderm is the starting point for the smooth muscle protocol.
The paper's figure text describes the cells as CD31+, CD34+, KDR+, CD105+, vWF+ and negative for CD43/CD45.
pitfalls: Confluency on day 1 is the main determinant of efficiency: too dense gives heavy death by day 4, too sparse a low yield.
Efficiency below 20% suggests inactive growth factors or wrong media; 20-50% usually means density or medium volume needs adjusting. Titrate density and GSK3 inhibitor dose per line.
A minor ACTA2+ mural population is always present before sorting.
unverified: Step values are taken from the authors' own Protocol Exchange write-up (Challet Meylan L, Patsch C, Thoma E; doi 10.1038/protex.2015.055 for endothelial cells, doi 10.1038/protex.2015.056 for smooth muscle cells) because the online Methods of the Nat Cell Biol paper could not be accessed.
Duration of endothelial expansion after sorting is not specified.

protocols.name: CHIR99021 alone in LaSR basal medium, CD34 sort on day 5
protocols.principle: Two days of Wnt activation in a minimal medium (Advanced DMEM/F12 with ascorbic acid) is enough to generate CD34+CD31+ endothelial progenitors without added VEGF or FGF; sorted progenitors mature into endothelial cells in EGM-2.

source.authors: Lian X, Bao X, Al-Ahmad A, et al.
source.title: Efficient differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells to endothelial progenitors via small-molecule activation of WNT signaling.

protocols.efficiency: More than 50% CD34+CD31+ progenitors reported in multiple lines (about 25% in the initial medium screen); >99% CD31+/VE-cadherin+ after purification and expansion
protocols.start_requirements: Singularised hPSCs seeded on Matrigel at 50,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 + 5 µM Y-27632 on day -3; mTeSR1 changed daily until day 0.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: LaSR basal medium (Advanced DMEM/F12 + 2.5 mM GlutaMAX + 60 µg/ml ascorbic acid)
actions: Replace mTeSR1 with LaSR basal + CHIR99021

stages.name: Endothelial progenitor specification
actions: Remove CHIR99021
On day 5 dissociate with Accutase (10 min) and purify CD34+ cells magnetically
stages.checkpoint: CD34+CD31+ cells by flow on day 5.

stages.name: Endothelial maturation
actions: Plate sorted CD34+ cells on collagen IV-coated dishes
stages.checkpoint: By day 15 cells express CD31, CD144, vWF, ICAM1 and KDR and have lost CD34.

tips: Seeding density strongly affects yield; the authors screened 12,000-300,000 cells/cm2.
Sorted cells went through about 20 population doublings over 2 months.
pitfalls: Basal medium matters: RPMI/B27 and serum-containing endothelial medium gave no CD34+CD31+ cells in this scheme.
Endogenous MEK signalling is required; MEK inhibition abolishes the progenitors.
The CD34+ fraction is bipotent and also gives smooth muscle cells in other media.

cell_types.notes: Plan on a purification step (CD144, CD31 or CD34 beads or FACS); unsorted cultures are overgrown by mural cells. hPSC-ECs are generic or embryonic-like rather than organ-specific and stop proliferating after a few passages. Orlova et al. 2014 Nat Protoc (PMID 24874816) is another widely used protocol that yields endothelial cells and pericytes from the same culture, but its step values could not be checked here.

cell_types.name: Vascular smooth muscle cells
cell_types.summary: Contractile cells of the vessel wall that set vascular tone and switch between contractile and synthetic states in disease. hPSC-derived smooth muscle cells are used to model aortopathies and atherosclerosis and to build vessel grafts and co-cultures with endothelium.
route: Lateral plate / paraxial mesoderm or neural crest
cell_types.maturation_note: PDGFRB+ cells by day 6; contractile proteins (CNN1, TAGLN, MYH11) accumulate over 1-2 further weeks and depend on the maturation medium.

morphology.endpoint: Elongated spindle cells growing in a hill-and-valley pattern; contractile-biased cultures are larger, flatter and slow-growing with visible filament bundles.

stages.label: Sparse hPSCs
stages.look: Single cells and small clusters after plating.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Flattened, proliferating loose sheet.

stages.label: Lateral mesoderm
stages.look: Confluent heterogeneous sheet.

stages.label: Mural progenitors
stages.look: Cells elongate and align after PDGF-BB.

stages.label: Smooth muscle cells
stages.look: Aligned spindle cells in hills and valleys.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Early marker; not specific on its own.

markers.name: MYH11

markers.name: CSPG4
markers.note: Small subpopulation (2-8%) in the Cheung protocol.

functional_assays: Contraction to carbachol, angiotensin II or endothelin-1
qc: Almost all cells PDGFRB+ and CD144-negative on day 6 (Patsch 2015)
>80% MYH11+/ACTA2+ after 12 days of PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1 (Cheung 2012)

protocols.name: CHIR99021 + BMP4 mesoderm, then PDGF-BB + Activin A (6 days)
protocols.principle: The same three-day CHIR99021 + BMP4 mesoderm used for endothelial cells is switched to PDGF-BB and Activin A, which gives almost exclusively PDGFRB+ mural cells; replating conditions then bias them to a synthetic or a contractile phenotype.

source.authors: Patsch C, Challet-Meylan L, Thoma EC, et al.
source.title: Generation of vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: Over 80% within six days (abstract); almost exclusively CD140b (PDGFRB)+ with virtually no CD144+ cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in mTeSR1 on Matrigel. Day 0: seed single cells at 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632.

stages.name: Plating
actions: Seed 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2

stages.name: Lateral mesoderm induction
stages.feeding: Three days with no medium change
actions: Use 3 ml per 12-well
Do not change medium

stages.name: Smooth muscle induction
actions: Feed 2 ml per 12-well daily
stages.checkpoint: PDGFRB+ spindle cells, CD144 negative.

stages.name: Replating and phenotype choice
actions: Seed 30,000 cells/cm2
Synthetic: gelatin-coated plates with PDGF-BB
Contractile: collagen-coated plates with Activin A + heparin
stages.checkpoint: Elongated ACTA2+ cells; contractile wells proliferate little.

tips: Residual CD144+ cells can be removed by MACS if needed.
Serum and high PDGF-BB were deliberately avoided, so cells proliferate slowly, especially under the contractile condition.
pitfalls: Pure populations of one phenotype are hard to maintain; with prolonged culture the synthetic phenotype dominates.
Density on day 1 controls efficiency, as for the endothelial arm.
unverified: Step values are taken from the authors' own Protocol Exchange write-up (Challet Meylan L, Patsch C, Thoma E; doi 10.1038/protex.2015.055 for endothelial cells, doi 10.1038/protex.2015.056 for smooth muscle cells) because the online Methods of the Nat Cell Biol paper could not be accessed.

protocols.name: Origin-specific smooth muscle via lateral plate mesoderm (PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1)
protocols.principle: hPSCs are first patterned into a defined embryonic intermediate (lateral plate mesoderm here; neuroectoderm or paraxial mesoderm in the alternative arms), then all intermediates are differentiated with PDGF-BB and TGF-beta1 for 12 days to give smooth muscle cells that retain origin-specific behaviour.

source.authors: Cheung C, Bernardo AS, Trotter MW, et al.
source.title: Generation of human vascular smooth muscle subtypes provides insight into embryological origin-dependent disease susceptibility.

protocols.efficiency: >80% MYH11+/ACTA2+ cells after 12 days of PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1 from all three intermediates
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in chemically defined medium (CDM) with Activin A and FGF2.

stages.name: Early mesoderm
actions: Change to CDM + FGF2 + LY294002 + BMP4

stages.name: Lateral plate mesoderm
actions: Change to FGF2 + high BMP4
stages.checkpoint: KDR and other lateral plate markers up; paraxial markers off.

stages.name: Smooth muscle differentiation
actions: Trypsinise the intermediate population and replate in PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1
Withdraw growth factors for at least 24 h before assays
stages.checkpoint: Early markers (ACTA2, TAGLN, CNN1) rise first; MYH11 peaks around days 9-12 of this step.

tips: Alternative origins: neuroectoderm with FGF2 12 ng/ml + SB431542 10 µM for 7 days; paraxial mesoderm with FGF2 20 ng/ml + LY294002 10 µM after the 36 h early-mesoderm step; both then get the same PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1 treatment.
A step-by-step version was published as Cheung et al. 2014 Nat Protoc (PMID 24675733, doi 10.1038/nprot.2014.059).

Choose the intermediate to match the embryonic origin of the vessel being modelled (for example neuroectoderm/neural crest for the ascending aorta and arch, paraxial mesoderm for the descending aorta).
pitfalls: A small fraction of cells (2-8%) express the pericyte marker CSPG4 (NG2) during differentiation.
The CDM system with Activin/FGF2 maintenance is different from mTeSR1/E8 culture; adaptation may be needed.
unverified: Duration of the paraxial mesoderm step is not stated explicitly in the sentence read (it parallels the 3.5-day lateral plate step).
The 2014 Nat Protoc version could not be accessed, so any refinements there are not included.

cell_types.notes: Smooth muscle identity is a spectrum: ACTA2 and TAGLN are also expressed by fibroblasts and pericytes, so include MYH11 and a contraction assay. Embryonic origin (lateral plate, paraxial mesoderm or neural crest) changes cell behaviour and should match the disease being modelled.

cell_types.name: Pericytes / mural cells
cell_types.summary: Mural cells wrapped around capillaries that stabilise the endothelium and regulate barrier function and blood flow. hPSC-derived pericyte-like cells are mainly used in blood-brain barrier and neurovascular models, vascular co-cultures and vascularised organoids.
cell_types.maturation_note: Marker-positive cells within 10 days by the mesoderm route and 22-25 days by the neural crest route; function is tested in endothelial co-culture.

morphology.endpoint: Flat, irregular stellate-to-spindle cells with long processes, growing as a loose monolayer; in co-culture they line up along endothelial cords.

stages.label: hPSCs
stages.look: Single-cell-plated hPSCs.

stages.label: Neural crest or mesoderm intermediate
stages.look: Small, migratory cells at high density; passaged repeatedly in the neural crest route.

stages.label: Sorted progenitors
stages.look: Sparse bipolar or stellate cells after replating.

stages.label: Pericyte-like cells
stages.look: Larger, flattened spindle and stellate cells with fine processes.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Used to sort neural crest on day 15; also found on mesodermal mesenchyme.

markers.name: B3GAT1
markers.note: Neural crest route only; absent in the mesoderm route.

markers.name: CSPG4
markers.note: Core pericyte marker; use together with PDGFRB.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Should be low; high levels indicate smooth-muscle-like cells.

Increase in endothelial barrier (TEER) in blood-brain barrier co-culture
Contraction or calcium response to vasoactive agents
qc: PDGFRB+ and NG2+ with low alpha-SMA (Gastfriend 2021)
PDGFRB+, NG2+, CD13+, CD146+ and CD34-negative by flow (Faal 2019)
Self-assembly with endothelial cords in co-culture

protocols.name: Brain pericyte-like cells via neural crest (E6-CSFD, then E6 + 10% FBS)
protocols.principle: Forebrain pericytes come from neural crest, so hPSCs are first converted to p75-NGFR+ HNK-1+ neural crest by Wnt activation with TGF-beta and BMP inhibition, sorted, and then pushed to NG2+ PDGFRB+ mural cells with serum.

source.authors: Gastfriend BD, Stebbins MJ, Du F, et al.
source.title: Differentiation of Brain Pericyte-Like Cells from Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neural Crest.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in E8 on Matrigel at about 70% confluence. Day -1: singularise with Accutase and seed 8.75 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate in E8 + 10 µM Y-27632.

stages.name: Neural crest induction and expansion
stages.base_medium: E6-CSFD (E6 medium with the five additives below)
actions: Replace E8 with E6-CSFD on day 0
Each time cells reach 100% confluence (first at about day 1-3) passage 1:6 with Accutase onto Matrigel
Keep a backup well at the first passage in case reattachment is poor
On day 15 isolate p75-NGFR+ cells with neural crest magnetic beads
stages.checkpoint: p75-NGFR+ HNK-1+ neural crest cells on day 15.

stages.name: Replating of sorted neural crest
actions: Seed sorted cells on uncoated tissue-culture plastic

stages.name: Pericyte differentiation
actions: Switch to E6 + 10% FBS
Continue for 6-9 days depending on the downstream use (day 22-25)
stages.checkpoint: NG2+ PDGFRB+ cells with low alpha-SMA.

materials: Neural Crest Stem Cell MicroBeads (anti-p75-NGFR) and MACS columns
tips: Original report: Stebbins MJ et al. 2019 Sci Adv (PMID 30891496, doi 10.1126/sciadv.aau7375).
Adding 10 µM Y-27632 at the first neural crest passage can rescue lines that reattach poorly.
Sorted neural crest can be expanded or frozen and differentiated later.
The cells express brain mural genes (ZIC1, FOXF2) and calponin/SM22-alpha but little alpha-SMA.
pitfalls: Some death after the first neural crest passage is normal; poor reattachment is the usual failure point.
Markers that cleanly separate pericytes from smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts are still incomplete, so describe the product as 'pericyte-like'.
unverified: Seeding density for the pericyte step is given in a table that was not captured.
The exact day of the switch from E6-CSFD + Y-27632 to E6 + 10% FBS after sorting is inferred as the day after plating.
No purity figure was captured from the text read.

protocols.name: Mesoderm route: 5 days mesoderm induction, 5 days pericyte medium
protocols.principle: hPSCs are converted to KDR+ mesoderm in a mesoderm induction medium for five days, then passaged into a commercial pericyte growth medium for five days; a parallel arm starts from CHIR99021-induced neural crest instead.

source.authors: Faal T, Phan DTT, Davtyan H, et al.
source.title: Induction of Mesoderm and Neural Crest-Derived Pericytes from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells to Study Blood-Brain Barrier Interactions.

protocols.efficiency: Surface PDGFRB, NG2, CD13 and CD146 at levels comparable to primary human brain vascular pericytes; CD34 negative
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs or iPSCs under feeder-free conditions (details in the paper's supplement).

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Culture hPSCs in MIM for 5 days
stages.checkpoint: KDR+ cells expressing MIXL1 and TBXT; HNK-1 negative.

stages.name: Pericyte induction
actions: Passage the mesoderm cells into pericyte medium
Maintain for 5 days, then expand
stages.checkpoint: PDGFRB+, NG2+, CD13+, CD146+ cells; CD34 negative; low alpha-SMA.

materials: Antibodies: KDR, HNK-1, CD271, PDGFRB, NG2, CD13, CD146, CD34
tips: The neural crest arm of the same paper uses a CHIR99021-containing neural crest medium for 5 days before the same pericyte medium.
Both pericyte populations increased endothelial tube formation and barrier properties in co-culture.
pitfalls: CD271 alone does not prove neural crest identity; it is also on mesoderm-derived mesenchymal progenitors.
The pericyte medium is proprietary, so the active factors are undefined.
unverified: Supplier and composition of the mesodermal induction medium, coating, seeding densities and feeding schedule are in the supplement, which was not read.

protocols.name: Clonal mesenchymoangioblast colonies, then PDGF-BB and pericyte medium
protocols.principle: Primitive posterior mesoderm is taken after two days of differentiation and grown in semisolid medium with FGF2, where mesenchymoangioblasts form compact colonies; colonies are then plated with PDGF-BB to make proliferative immature pericytes that can be matured into capillary-type or arteriolar-type pericytes.

source.authors: Kumar A, D'Souza SS, Moskvin OV, et al.
source.title: Specification and Diversification of Pericytes and Smooth Muscle Cells from Mesenchymoangioblasts.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs differentiated for 2 days to mesoderm, either on OP9 stromal cells or in the authors' chemically defined conditions (BMP4, Activin A, FGF2).

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: OP9 co-culture or chemically defined medium
actions: Differentiate hPSCs for 2 days
Prepare a single-cell suspension on day 2
stages.checkpoint: APLNR+ PDGFRA+ primitive posterior mesoderm.

stages.name: Mesenchymoangioblast colony formation
actions: Plate 0.5-2 x 10^4 cells/ml
On day 12 of colony culture pick colonies, or dilute 1:5 in DMEM/F12 and collect colonies >100 µm on a 100 µm strainer
stages.checkpoint: Compact spheroid colonies.

stages.name: Pericyte specification
actions: Plate colonies on dishes coated with fibronectin (3 µg/ml) and collagen I (10 µg/ml)
stages.checkpoint: Colonies attach and spread.

stages.name: Immature pericyte expansion
stages.feeding: Until confluent (14 days), then passage every 3 days
actions: Dissociate with Accutase and replate on fibronectin/collagen
stages.checkpoint: Confluent monolayer of proliferative NG2+ PDGFRB+ CD13+ CD146+ cells.

stages.name: Optional maturation

factors.name: EGF2 as written in the paper (PC2 only)

actions: Then split 1:5 and culture 4 more days in Pericyte Medium

materials: OP9 cells or defined mesoderm medium
tips: The same colonies give smooth muscle cells if plated in EGM-2 with sphingosylphosphorylcholine (2 µM) and TGF-beta3 (2 ng/ml) for 6 days.
Immature pericytes could be cultured for up to 12 passages, with senescence appearing from passages 8-12.
pitfalls: Long and technically specialised (semisolid clonogenic culture, colony picking); choose it when clonal origin or pericyte subtype matters.
CF-SFM and M-SFEM are in-house formulations defined in earlier papers from the same laboratory.
unverified: Concentrations and medium for the 2-day mesoderm induction were not captured (given by reference to earlier papers).
The paper lists 'EGF2 (2 ng/mL)' in the PC2 maturation mix; whether this means EGF or FGF2 could not be resolved.
No yield or purity figure captured.

cell_types.notes: There is no single definitive pericyte marker, and published 'pericytes' differ by route (neural crest versus mesoderm) and medium, so state the route and show a marker panel plus an endothelial co-culture assay. Orlova et al. 2014 Nat Protoc (PMID 24874816) derives pericytes from the CD31-negative fraction of an endothelial differentiation; its step values could not be checked here.

cell_types.name: Blood vessel organoids
cell_types.summary: Self-organising 3D capillary networks of endothelial cells and pericytes wrapped in a basement membrane. They are used to model diabetic vasculopathy and other microvascular disease, to study vessel-wall biology, and as a source of human vessels for transplantation or for vascularising other organoids.
cell_types.maturation_note: Networks form about 5 days after embedding; extracted organoids can be kept for up to 3 months and mature further after transplantation.

morphology.endpoint: Before extraction, a dense core with fine branching sprouts radiating into the gel; after extraction, a translucent sphere that needs CD31/PDGFRB/collagen IV whole-mount staining to show the network.

stages.label: Aggregates
stages.look: Small round aggregates forming in suspension.

stages.label: Mesoderm aggregates
stages.look: Aggregates enlarge and become rougher and darker.

stages.label: Embedded in gel
stages.look: Aggregates sit in the collagen I-Matrigel gel; first sprouts appear within days.

stages.label: Sprouting vascular network
stages.look: Branching tube-like sprouts extend radially from the core.

stages.label: Free-floating organoid
stages.look: Extracted networks compact into smooth spheres.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: PECAM1
markers.note: Whole-mount staining shows the capillary network.

markers.name: COL4A1
markers.note: Continuous sheath around vessels; thickens under diabetic conditions.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Check if haematopoietic contamination matters for your assay.

functional_assays: Whole-mount imaging of CD31+ network with PDGFRB+ pericyte coverage and collagen IV sheath
Basement membrane thickening under high glucose + cytokines
Perfusion after transplantation into immunodeficient mice
qc: Sprouting visible within days of embedding and networks established around day 18 (Wimmer 2019)
CD31+ tubes covered by PDGFRB+ pericytes and a collagen IV basement membrane

protocols.name: Mesoderm aggregates embedded in collagen I-Matrigel with VEGF-A and FGF-2
protocols.principle: hPSC aggregates are driven to mesoderm with CHIR99021 and to vascular lineages with BMP4, VEGF-A and FGF-2; embedding in a collagen I-Matrigel gel with high VEGF-A and FGF-2 lets endothelial cells sprout into capillary networks covered by pericytes and basement membrane, which are then cut out and kept as free-floating organoids.

source.authors: Wimmer RA, Leopoldi A, Aichinger M, et al.
source.title: Human blood vessel organoids as a model of diabetic vasculopathy.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells (brief EDTA then Accutase); 2 x 10^5 cells per well of an ultra-low-attachment 6-well plate.

stages.name: Aggregation
stages.base_medium: Differentiation medium (DMEM/F12 + 20% KnockOut Serum Replacement + GlutaMAX + NEAA)
actions: Plate 2 x 10^5 cells per ultra-low-attachment well
stages.checkpoint: Small round aggregates.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Add CHIR99021 to the aggregates

stages.name: Vascular specification
actions: Refresh factors every second day

stages.name: Endothelial enrichment

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: Raises endothelial yield and limits excess pericyte differentiation

actions: Switch to VEGF-A + FGF-2 + SB431542

stages.name: Sprouting in 3D gel
stages.base_medium: Differentiation medium over a Matrigel:collagen I (1:1) gel
actions: Embed aggregates in the gel on day 13 and overlay with medium
stages.checkpoint: Vessel sprouts radiate from each aggregate; networks established around day 18.

stages.name: Free-floating organoids
stages.base_medium: Differentiation medium with VEGF-A and FGF-2
actions: Cut individual networks out of the gel
Transfer one per well to 96-well ultra-low-attachment U-bottom plates
stages.checkpoint: Networks round up into spherical organoids; culturable for up to 3 months.

tips: A stepwise, optimised version by the same authors is Wimmer et al. 2019 Nat Protoc (PMID 31554955, doi 10.1038/s41596-019-0213-z); read it before starting, since it differs in detail from this first description.
For the diabetic vasculopathy model the authors exposed organoids to high glucose plus inflammatory cytokines and scored collagen IV basement-membrane thickening.
Organoids transplanted under the mouse kidney capsule became perfused and formed arteries, arterioles and venules.
pitfalls: Matrigel and collagen lots vary and the gel must be kept cold and mixed quickly; sprouting quality depends on it.
The first description starts from a bulk suspension of aggregates in a 6-well plate, so aggregate size is not tightly controlled.
unverified: Values are from the Nature 2019 Methods; the Nat Protoc version could not be accessed, so its (reportedly shorter and more defined) schedule is not given.
Feeding details for days 0-3 and the medium/factor concentrations after extraction (assumed unchanged from the gel stage) were not stated explicitly in the text read.
The end day of the final stage (30) is nominal; the paper states only that organoids can be kept for up to 3 months.
No efficiency figure (endothelial/pericyte percentages) was captured.

cell_types.notes: A technically demanding 3D protocol: outcome depends on aggregate size, the collagen/Matrigel gel and growth-factor quality. Only the original Nature description could be verified here; follow the authors' Nat Protoc paper for the current step-by-step version.

cell_types.name: Cardiac organoids / cardioids
cell_types.summary: Self-organising 3D heart-like structures containing cardiomyocytes together with epicardial, endocardial/endothelial and stromal cells, often with internal chambers or cavities. They are used to study early human heart development, congenital heart defects, maternal-diabetes and drug effects, and injury responses.
cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 6-7; chambers and multi-lineage organisation by day 10-15; cultures have been kept beating for at least 8 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A single beating spheroid per well, with darker dense myocardium and paler cavities or an outer translucent layer; Matrigel-embedded versions show concentric layers.

stages.label: Aggregate formation
stages.look: One compact, smooth-edged hPSC aggregate at the bottom of each U-well.

stages.label: Mesoderm aggregate
stages.look: Aggregate swells and the edge becomes less sharp after CHIR99021.

stages.label: Cardiac mesoderm
stages.look: Larger, darker spheroid; cavities start to appear.

stages.label: Beating organoid
stages.look: Rhythmic contraction of part or all of the spheroid.

stages.label: Chambered organoid
stages.look: Beating spheroid with internal lumens and an outer epicardial layer.

markers.note: High at day 0; should be lost within the first days of differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Second pluripotency check; should be absent in the finished culture.

markers.name: HAND1
markers.note: First-heart-field marker; HAND2 marks second heart field.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Outer epicardial cells (after the day-7 CHIR pulse in the Lewis-Israeli method).

markers.name: TJP1

markers.note: Expected in heart-forming organoids (foregut endoderm) but an unwanted lineage in pure cardiac organoids.

Response to teratogens or metabolic stress (for example high glucose)
